column1:
Major Risks;
• Health and safety within
our business premises
• Vulnerabilities as a
result of working from
home arrangements
• Exposure to fraud with
increased digitized
transactions
column2:
In the wake of COVID-19, the Group has
been exposed to an increasing number
of reputational threats.
Such include;
1. Increased possibility of infections
among our customers and staff within
our business premises,
2. System infiltration by external players
who may exploit vulnerabilities within
remote working arrangements and
3. Possible cases of fraud on our clients
as a result of the digitalization of most
transactions.
Such threats typically result in negative
publicity if not well managed. As a market
leader and systemically important
institution, reputational issues are
handled with utmost significance thereby
protecting the interests of stakeholders
at all times.
column3:
Reputational Risk is therefore managed in the
following ways;
1. The Board periodically reviews the Reputational
Risk profile of the institution, areas of improvement
are identified on a continous basis and actioned.
2. The Group has established service level agreements
at all points of stakeholder engagement.
3. In an era of rapid technological advancements, the
Group proactively monitors online content related to
all its subsidiaries to avert any instances of potential
reputational damage.
